description: "When analyzing any video Nick sends, extract and look at one frame for EVERY second, never sampled (not every 20s); redo if sampled"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  modified: 2026-09-17T14:48:35.470Z
---

Video analysis rule: extract one frame per second (`ffmpeg -vf fps=1`) and look at every one, alongside the transcript. Sampling (I used one frame per 20 seconds on 2026-09-17) is not allowed; Nick said "the rule is every single second" and had both videos redone.

**Why:** on-screen text (prompt cards, tweets, lower thirds, terminal output) often shows for only a few seconds and carries detail the speech does not.

**How to apply:** frames at 640px, tiled 16 per sheet (4x4, 480px tiles) with a mm:ss label burned in via PIL (homebrew ffmpeg has no drawtext); fan sheets out to parallel viewer agents that must open every sheet in order and list the sheets opened. Get captions with yt-dlp when the video is on YouTube.

Related: [[triple-check-before-showing]], [[verify-before-asserting]]

Not enough for fast cuts (Nick, 2026-10-10, Base44): shots shorter than a second fall between 1 fps frames and cut
detectors merge them. Base44's first 1.62 s holds 8 shots and 7 people, including a posed pair I missed. Read every frame
(24 fps) of any section with sub-second cuts before mapping it.

Do not present manual setup as completed installation.\n\nConnect a desktop MCP client to a dedicated background Blender process on the same computer:\n\nDesktop client → stdio → fnf-blender-mcp → process pipes → Blender Python / bpy.\n\nUse **Higgsfield use Blender** as the display name and `higgsfield-use-blender` as the server identifier. No add-on, HTTP listener, WebSocket or cloud account is required for local scene operations.\n\nEach MCP session owns its own scene. Commands preserve that scene in memory until the connection closes; save needed work with `bl_save_project`. This integration cannot read unsaved work in an already-open Blender window. To edit that work, first save it in the desktop application, then load the file with `bl_open_project`. To inspect results in the UI, open the saved output file separately.\n\nUse `fnf-blender-mcp@latest`; version 0.1.0 requires an add-on and cannot provide this workflow. # Imagine — Visual Creation Suite

## Modules
Call read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance:
- `diagram` — SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams
- `mockup` — UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards
- `interactive` — interactive explainers with controls
- `chart` — charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth)
- `art` — illustration and generative art
Pick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance.

**Complexity budget — hard limits:**
- Box subtitles: ≤5 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below — not the box.
- Colors: ≤2 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp.
- Horizontal tier: ≤4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes → shrink to ≤110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams.

If you catch yourself writing "click to learn more" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything.

**Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `<h2 class="sr-only">` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `<title>` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.)

You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat.

## Core Design System

These rules apply to ALL use cases.

### Philosophy
- **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins.
- **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces.
- **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text.
- **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it.

### Streaming
Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early.
- **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last.
- **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately.
- Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream.
- Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS.
- Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead.

### Rules
- No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming)
- No font-size below 11px
- No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths.
- No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects
- No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg)
- **Typography**: The default font is the person's Interface font, usually Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `fon ...[cut]
```

- **Blender does the previs only.** One chat request builds boxes and a camera path, then one fix at a time. His example at 12:56: "Hold the fight reveal for one more second" became camera key 601 to 625.
- **Seedance 2.5 does the look.** The previs clip goes in as the motion reference, the storyboard images as the look. Our Higgsfield connector already has this (checked today: video references, 4 to 30 s).
- **The page shows three things per shot, side by side on one timeline:** storyboard, locked previs, AI look clip (his layout at 13:04). An approved camera move is saved and reused, as in his one previs for three products.
- **Install the Higgsfield Blender plugin.** It is not on the Mac today (add-ons are HumGen3D, mpfb and the MCP bridge). It adds phone camera recording by QR code, and needs a Blender with a screen; the 3D box has no Blender.

- **Final shot:** the page outputs the finished clip and animators only fix what drifts.

**Based on:** all 983 one-per-second frames read by me, the YouTube captions of the same video (id PEEBZwGetyc, 983 s), and the Mac, box and Higgsfield connector checked today, 12 Nov. The dollar figures are his on-screen claims for one ad.

# AOW ops agents: brief for a new session

Written 10 Nov 2026. Paths below were checked to exist that day; what is inside them was not read in depth. Read them before building.

## The goal
Operations management agents for The Art of War, like the [other project] for [other project]. The interface and its agents and
subagents break information silos and get the important operational info to the CEO. The team has scriptwriters,
animators, editors and others. We have no Asana, Slack or other access to their tools.

## Rule: tailor, don't rebuild
Use the infra we already have.

- **[other project] (pattern to copy):** `~/Desktop/[other project] (1)/repos/[other project]-company-agent`. Look at `agent/` (agent.ts, instructions, tools, connections, channels, skills) and `companybrain/`. Specs are in `~/Desktop/[other project] (1)/[other project]/`, starting with `[other project]-MASTER-SPEC.md`. Rules to keep:
  - Every answer either carries a link or says "I don't know" honestly.
  - Read-only first. Any action needs approval from the person who asked.
  - Evals gate every change.
- **Spiti (the live interface):** `~/Library/CloudStorage/[email]/My Drive/Nick-AE/Desktop-2026-11-07/spiti`. It holds server.py (port 8560, localhost only), brain.py, funnel.py, agents.json, and static/index.html, agent.html and funnel.html. It shows agents as nodes on a sphere.
  - `~/Desktop/spiti` is an older, near-empty copy.
- **PlotPointe (the real AOW scripts data):**
  - Bot code on the Mac: `.../Nick-AE/aow-funnel/1-scripts/telegram/`. The live copy is on the server at root@37.27.148.115, service `aow-bot`.
  - Docs, versions, comments, approvals and costs live in its data and state files.
  - Never restart or touch `aow-bot` from the ops work.
- **YouTube tracker (real performance data):**
  - Code: `.../Nick-AE/aow-funnel/ledger/tracker.py`.
  - Database: `~/aow-data/tracker.sqlite`. It was last written on 7 Nov, so check why polling stopped.
- **Stage folders:** `.../Nick-AE/aow-funnel/` has 1-scripts, 2-images, 3-animation, 4-edit and 5-review-post.

## Proposed shape (agreed in principle with Nick, details open)
- One agent per department: Scripts (PlotPointe), Performance (tracker), and Production for animation, edit, and review and post (stage folders).
- A Chief of Staff on top. It writes the CEO's daily brief: what moved, what's blocked, and what needs a decision.
- Cross-department flags are the point, for example:
  - an approved script with no animator after N days
  - a clip spiking, so the writer should do a follow-up
  - a writer stuck on version 6
- Tools we can't reach (Asana, Slack, animation tools) appear as "connect to unlock" slots that say what each would add.
- Never present fake data as theirs. Any sample data is labelled as sample.

## Open questions for Nick (ask first)
1. The team roster: roles and roughly how many of each.
2. What the CEO asks about week to week.
3. Where it lives: inside PlotPointe, or its own page (Spiti-style).

## Working rules
- Follow `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, "Verified or it doesn't ship".
- No em or en dashes.
- Short replies, ending with a bold one-sentence summary.
- Show concept options before building any page.

the fact sheet. Models research, write prompts and judge images; this code decides counts, references and what passes.
Everything is kept in research/visuals/<doc id>.json, which PlotPointe draws.

### CLAUDE 2026-11-12T18:23

**The page is a new "Animate" step after Visuals in PlotPointe: the storyboard image gives the look, a Blender scene in the page locks the camera, and Seedance 2.5 makes the clip.** Blender in your own page is possible without installing Blender anywhere, because our Higgsfield connector has a hosted one.

- **The storyboard is ready to feed it.** The Bat Bombs has 15 shots over 30 s and The Captain Who Sank His Own Ship has 19 over 37 s, each with its words, prompt and image; four other storyboards show "failed".
- **Blender in the page means a 3D view, not the full Blender program.** You orbit, press play and see the camera path, and changes go through chat. The video is the same: his Blender was the desktop app, and only the camera view ran in a browser (10:20).
- **The hosted Blender is Higgsfield "3D Jutsu".** It builds the scene by script, hands back a web 3D file and a .blend, and sends a render straight to Seedance 2.5 in 9:16, 4 to 30 s. The 3D box cannot do this itself: it has no Blender.
- **PlotPointe already runs on GPT-6 Astra**, the agent the video recommends for this, so no agent switch is needed.

For the question in the box:

- **Only camera shots (my pick):** a 2 s shot of a captain on the bridge animates straight from its storyboard image. Blender opens only where the camera travels, like a dive over the ship. Building 15 to 19 Blender scenes per short is slow and mostly wasted.
- **Every shot:** every shot gets a 3D scene and a locked camera, with more control and far more build time.

**Based on:** the live PlotPointe code and storyboard files on the 3D box, read-only today 12 Nov (the bot was not touched), the Higgsfield tool descriptions read today, and the video.

**To verify, for you only:**
- Credit cost per clip on our account.
- Whether the 3D view can sit inside the PlotPointe page or only opens as a Higgsfield link.
- Whether the camera move survives in the web 3D file.
- Seedance's minimum is 4 s and your shots are about 2 s, so each clip is cut down or several shots share one clip. Neither is tested.

=== SUBSCRIPTION_SETUP.md
# Start here: PlotPointe with your ChatGPT subscription

Prepared 11 November 2026. This release defaults to Codex CLI, not the paid API.
Use the existing Hetzner server and its existing Claude connection. No new server needed.

## Give this instruction to the connected Claude

Read this file and INSTALL_FOR_CLAUDE.md. Stage this release in a NEW directory, preserve
my live code/data/credentials, and run the subscription check as the existing bot service
user. Let me complete the ChatGPT device login in my browser. After a successful real
research/writing smoke test, integrate the new writer into the current platform, preserving
changes made today outside the replaced ideation/writing pipeline. Back up first and
replace the existing service, never run a second Telegram poller. Verify a real story in
PlotPointe, Google Docs editing, Compare drafts, and saving feedback. Report actual results,
not just unit tests. Do not use the paid API or change the requested model silently.

## Fast test on Hetzner

Run as the same Linux user that runs the existing bot. Start from the extracted `1-scripts`
directory. Use the existing Python virtual environment, or create a staging environment:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
npm install -g @openai/codex
bash scripts/subscription-check.sh
```

If Codex is already installed and supports `exec --ignore-user-config`, skip npm install.
If npm requires admin permissions, install under the service user's own prefix instead;
do not change system permissions. Set AOW_CODEX_BIN to the absolute resulting binary path.

The check creates a dedicated private `~/.plotpointe-codex` login directory. It opens the
supported device login flow if needed. Nick completes the browser login himself. Never
print, upload or share auth.json. If using an existing Codex login, explicitly set
AOW_CODEX_HOME to that writable credential directory before running the check.

The check then makes one tiny real model call and runs research plus two drafts for
HMS Amethyst's escape. To choose another topic:

```bash
bash scripts/subscription-check.sh "A different historical event"
```

It prints the temporary result directory. It does not start the bot, send Telegram
messages, write Google Docs, change live data, or modify the service. It uses subscription
allowance. Inspect result.json and the original cited sources before publication.

If device login is unavailable, enable device code login in ChatGPT security settings,
or use `CODEX_HOME="$HOME/.plotpointe-codex" codex login` with the official SSH browser
callback flow. Complete login as the service user, not root if the bot runs as another user.

## Required service settings after the test succeeds

Keep existing BOT_DATA, BOT_TOKEN_FILE, Google credentials, port and public URL. Add:

```text
AOW_PROVIDER=codex
AOW_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-6-astra
AOW_CODEX_BIN=/absolute/path/to/codex
AOW_CODEX_HOME=/home/SERVICE_USER/.plotpointe-codex
AOW_CODEX_TIMEOUT=600
PLOTPOINTE_START_BOT=1
```

Use the actual service username and executable path. Explicitly retain
PLOTPOINTE_PANEL_PORT=8770 and the existing PLOTPOINTE_APP_URL if those are the current
live values. New unconfigured launches default to localhost:18770 and cannot start
Telegram polling without PLOTPOINTE_START_BOT=1.

### CLAUDE 2026-11-12T18:35

**Your idea works if you flip it: PlotPointe plugs into each person's own Claude or ChatGPT app, not their chat inside our page.** I checked both sites today and neither allows itself to be shown inside another website, so "their login on one half of our page" is blocked at the door.

- **You already have the plug.** PlotPointe has its own connector on the box (`plotpointe_mcp.py`) that a person adds to their ChatGPT and signs in to. Today it hands over scripts and reads back your edits; Blender tools would be added to it.
- **The Blender half can sit beside their chat.** Higgsfield's connector already shows a live 3D scene panel inside the chat this way, so the split screen you pictured is possible there.
- **There is no cursor to track with a Blender MCP or CLI.** The AI runs Blender by commands and nobody moves a mouse. What we get is stronger: every request they typed, every Blender command and every version of the scene, in order.
- **A real cursor only exists if people model by hand.** That means streaming the full Blender program from a rented graphics machine per person, which is the heavy and costly route.

For the question in the box:

- **Their app + connector (my pick):** an animator opens their own ChatGPT, types "block the dock shot from storyboard image 4", the scene appears beside the chat, and PlotPointe saves each step. They pay for their own subscription and we host no Blender screens.
- **All on our page:** we build our own chat and stream Blender to the browser. We pay for the AI per use and a graphics machine per person, and in return we get cursor and screen recording.

Either way, tell the animators their steps are recorded.

**Based on:** the headers claude.ai and chatgpt.com sent today, 12 Nov; PlotPointe's connector and setup files on the box, read-only; and the Higgsfield tool descriptions.

**To verify, for you only:**
- Whether Anthropic and OpenAI allow a hosted product to run on each person's subscription login. I have not checked their terms.
- Whether our own connector can show a 3D panel in both Claude and ChatGPT the way Higgsfield's does.
- For hand modelling, whether a small Blender add-on can log every action. I believe so but have not tested it.

### CLAUDE 2026-11-12T18:52

**No, I would not put a chat at the centre of this page. With your three goals, the chat works against the second one: if the animator builds by typing to an AI, we record the AI's work and not the animator's craft, so PlotPointe learns nothing new.**

- **Goal 1, faster:** a button, not a chat. PlotPointe prepares the starting scene from the storyboard (camera matched to the picture, characters and props placed, shot length set from the narration), so the animator never opens an empty scene.
- **Goal 2, learning:** record what the animator changes by hand. The difference between our starting scene and their finished one is the lesson, and it is exactly the detail work we get wrong today.
- **Goal 3, slow laptops:** run the full Blender on a cloud machine and show it in the browser. The laptop only displays a video stream, and because the machine is ours we can record every action.
- **This reverses my last pick.** "Their own app plus our connector" suits writers who work in chat. Animators work with their hands, so the hosted page fits them.

Example of what we would learn: PlotPointe places the ship, the animator scales it up and adds deck detail, and that correction is saved against that storyboard picture for next time.

If you still want typing, keep it as one small notes line where the animator says why they changed something, such as "ship too small". That labels the recording for training.

**To verify, for you only:**
- Cost of a cloud graphics machine per animator per working day. My October notes say about $0.74 an hour on RunPod; not rechecked.
- Whether streamed Blender feels responsive enough to animate in. It needs a real test with one animator.
- Whether a Blender add-on can log every action. I believe so but have not tested it.

The search turned up a few usable paths for running Blender's GUI in a browser, with Selkies as the main option.

- **Selkies is the streaming layer.** It is an open-source low-latency high-performance Linux-native GPU/CPU-accelerated WebRTC HTML5 remote desktop streaming platform, and it streams a Linux X11 desktop or Docker/Kubernetes container to a recent web browser. Its NVENC hardware encoding is only supported in GPUs listed as supporting H.264 in NVIDIA's encode/decode matrix.
- **KasmVNC is the fallback.** It is a WebSocket-based HTML5 interface. It can be enabled in place of Selkies by setting KASMVNC_ENABLE to true. KasmVNC does not support audio forwarding, but it can help with troubleshooting.
- **Networking caveats.** Self-hosted WebRTC needs a relay: a TURN server is required because you are self-hosting WebRTC. Also, only one web browser can be connected at a time with the Selkies WebRTC interface.
- **Container images exist.** The Selkies project publishes a NVIDIA GLX desktop image. One guide shows running it with a restart policy and opening a browser at localhost:8080. The National Research Platform docs describe GPU-accelerated GUI desktop containers that support OpenGL and Vulkan, which Blender's viewport needs.
- **Ready-made Blender options.** A Railway template runs the full desktop Blender application in the cloud, streamed through the linuxserver.io Selkies web interface. However, its description says the session is GPU-less, so it may not suit GPU-accelerated viewport or Cycles work. Vagon also offers a hosted browser-streamed Blender, though the results don't say what stack it uses.

Search results don't give a complete recipe for logging every user operator, but they do point to a few usable routes and some limits.

- **Info editor log:** The Info editor logs the executed operators as well as errors, warnings, and informational messages. The Python-side equivalent is `window_manager.operators`, which a Blender developer on the mailing list described as a log of executed operators.
- **Limits of that log:** The same mailing list post says this log doesn't provide enough information to reliably reconstruct a sequence of user actions. It works for seeing when an operator finished, not for recording what the user did.
- **No API signal for invocation:** A separate post on the list says developers had found no method available through the python api that advises the user has invoked an operator, at least as of that thread (2016).
- **Modal operators:** Modal operators are a gap. One Blender developer doc notes that while a modal operator runs, no auto-saves or undo pushes are performed by Blender.
- **Handlers:** A Blender feature request about Python hooks on operators says hooks are implemented for all Blender operators, and such freedom can bring bad consequences, first of all in performance. That thread is old and was still open when the result was indexed, so treat it as background rather than current API documentation. I did not find details on `bpy.app.handlers` coverage for operators in these results.
- **Logging to a file:** For writing logs to disk, a Blender developer blog post says the approach is standard Python: add a handler that saves the log to a file using the `logging` module.
- **Known bug:** A Blender bug report says the Python ops log may stop populating when a startup file was saved by a version before a certain commit, and works with a fresh configuration. Check this if your log is empty.

Practical takeaway: `window_manager.operators` or the Info log can show which operators ran, but not a reliable user-action sequence. For full capture, you would probably need to combine a handler or add-on hook with a file logger, then test it against modal operators and older startup files. The results don't confirm a complete, supported method, so verify against the current `bpy` docs for your Blender version.

### CLAUDE 2026-11-12T19:00

**Then the hosted route fits, and the first step is one small test: Blender running on a rented cloud machine, shown in your browser, with you animating in it for ten minutes.** That one test answers the question the whole page depends on: does it feel smooth enough to animate in.

- **How it runs:** an open-source streamer called Selkies sends the Blender screen to a browser tab. It allows one person per machine, so each animator gets their own while working.
- **Correction to what I said earlier:** Blender's own action log is not a full record of hand work. It lists commands that finished but misses the dragging and posing, which is most of animating.
- **So the recording is two things we control:** a video of the screen, and a copy of the scene saved every few seconds, so we can compare what changed. The action log is a bonus on top.
- **Cost:** under $1 for the hour by every price I found ($0.34 to $0.74 an hour for the graphics card). I would set a hard stop at $3 and one hour. The box's own limits are $20 a day and $40 a month.

What you would do in the test: open a link, pose a simple figure and move the camera, then tell me if it lags. Afterwards I show you the recording and what the scene comparison caught.

**Based on:** a web search today (I read the summaries, not every page in full), the spending limits and cloud tool on the box read today, and your answer that animators work by hand in Blender.

- Whether the streamer needs an extra relay service to reach your browser; the docs say it usually does.
- Lag from Cyprus, which the test itself measures.

- tool `Write`: `{"file_path": "/Users/nick/Projects/plotpointe-animate/tools/build_data.py", "content": "\"\"\"Turn one PlotPointe storyboard file into the data the Animate page reads.\n\nIn:  data/<name>.json   exactly as PlotPointe saved it in research/visuals/<doc id>.json\n     data/img/shot_NN.png, data/img/ent_<id>.png   the images, downloaded once\nOut: data/img/*.jpg     smaller copies the page loads fast\n     data/story.js      window.STORY = {...}; a plain script so the page also opens straight from the file\n\nWords, prompts, names and looks are copied as they are, never rewritten.\n\"\"\"\nimport json\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nIMG = ROOT / \"data\" / \"img\"\nWORDS_PER_SECOND = 3.9   # the same number PlotPointe uses in telegram/visuals.py\n\n\ndef jpg(stem):\n    \"\"\"Make data/img/<stem>.jpg from the png once; return the page path, or None when there is no picture.\"\"\"\n    png, out = IMG / f\"{stem}.png\", IMG / f\"{stem}.jpg\"\n    if not out.exists():\n        if not png.exists():\n            return None\n        subprocess.run([\"sips\", \"-s\", \"format\", \"jpeg\", \"-s\", \"formatOptions\", \"82\", str(png), \"--out\", str(out)],\n                       check=True, capture_output=True)\n    return f\"data/img/{stem}.jpg\"\n\n\ndef build(name):\n    v = json.loads((ROOT / \"data\" / f\"{name}.json\").read_text())\n    story = {\n        \"doc\": v[\"doc\"], \"title\": v[\"title\"], \"seconds\": v[\"seconds\"],\n        \"entities\": [{\"id\": e[\"id\"], \"kind\": e[\"kind\"], \"name\": e[\"name\"], \"look\": e[\"look\"],\n                      \"image\": jpg(f\"ent_{e['id']}\")} for e in v[\"entities\"]],\n        \"shots\": [{\"words\": s[\"words\"], \"entities\": s[\"entities\"], \"prompt\": s[\"prompt\"],\n                   \"seconds\": round(len(s[\"words\"].split()) / WORDS_PER_SECOND, 1),\n                   \"image\": jpg(f\"shot_{i + 1:02d}\")} for i, s in enumerate(v[\"shots\"])],\n    }\n    (ROOT / \"data\" / \"story.js\").write_text(\"window.STORY = \" + json.dumps(story, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + \";\\n\")\n    return story\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    s = build(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else \"bat_bombs\")\n    print(f\"{s['title']}: {len(s['shots'])} shots, {len(s['entities'])} entities, \"\n          f\"{sum(1 for x in s['shots'] if x['image'])} shot pictures, {sum(1 for x in s['entities'] if x['image'])} entity pictures\")\n"}`

### CLAUDE 2026-11-12T19:24

**It has two real jobs: it tells the animator what this shot needs without leaving Blender, and it cuts the recording into labelled pieces so PlotPointe can learn from them. About half of what is in it today earns its place; the rest is duplicate.**

- **Faster for the animator:** the narration line the shot plays under, the shot's length, and the cast with their reference pictures. Without it they switch to the Visuals page or the script doc to look these up.
- **The training label:** the step button marks when work on each shot starts and ends. Without that, a recording is one long session and we cannot tell which minutes belong to "shot 8, the canister". The notes line adds the reason for a change, such as "camera lower so the canister fills the frame".
- **The speed button:** "Prepare starting scene" is where the time saving will come from once it is real. Today it only changes the label.
- **What is duplicate:** the Previous and Next links repeat the shot strip, and the long "what the picture shows" text was written for the image maker, not for an animator.

It does nothing for the slow-laptop goal; that comes only from running Blender in the cloud.

My view: animators want every pixel for Blender, so this column should fold away while they animate and open when they move to the next shot. I would keep the narration, cast, step button and notes, and drop the two duplicates.

### CLAUDE 2026-11-12T19:49

**Yes: the animator presses Generate on a storyboard shot, and the scene you spent today recreating by hand appears in Blender on the right as a real scene they can orbit, grab and animate. The button is today's work, turned into something every animator gets in one press.**

Your work is not gone. I checked just now:

- **In Drive** (`Nick-AE/Desktop-2026-11-12/navy_shots`): four scene files (officer, dock, cruiser, carrier with battleship), each with its storyboard picture and a compare sheet.
- **On the box:** the builders, plus a library (`officer.blend`) and scenes that use it (`SCENE_officer`, `SCENE_dock`). Files there were still being written at 20:55, so another session is working on it and I left it alone.

How this makes the animator faster:

- **They start from a built scene, not an empty one.** Your dock sheet shows it: the storyboard beside the built dock, with the officer standing in it and the camera pushing in over 240 frames. The animator opens that and starts animating.
- **Each thing is built once and reused.** In The Bat Bombs the bats are in 8 of the 15 shots and the air base in 7. Today's work already has this shape, with one officer in the library used by two scenes.
- **Their fixes teach the generator.** You said today the scenes get the shapes but miss the detail. The animator adds that detail, we record what they changed, and the next Generate starts closer.
- **Generate has to take minutes.** Today's route was slow, so reuse from the library is what keeps the button fast.

One gap to name plainly: "interactive on the right" means Blender itself is running there. In a web page that needs Blender on a cloud machine sent to the browser, which is the step after this one.

The free next step is the one in the box: put today's four navy storyboards into the page, with Generate showing your real built scenes. I would also rename the button to "Generate".

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""workbench: an always-on GPU for previews and stills (see renderdesk/workbench.py).
  workbench up                 rent it (stops itself after 30 idle minutes or 10 hours)
  workbench status             is it up, for how long, what it has cost
  workbench push DIR_OR_FILE   copy to the same absolute path on the pod
  workbench run 'COMMAND'      run there ($BLENDER is set)
  workbench pull REMOTE LOCAL  copy back
  workbench down               destroy it now and log its cost
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
from renderdesk import config, workbench as wb  # noqa: E402


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2 or sys.argv[1] in ("-h", "--help"):
        print(__doc__)
        return 0
    cfg = config.load()
    cmd, rest = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:]
    if cmd == "up":
        return wb.up(cfg)
    if cmd == "status":
        return wb.status(cfg)
    if cmd == "down":
        return wb.down(cfg)
    if cmd == "run" and rest:
        return wb.run(cfg, " ".join(rest))
    if cmd == "push" and rest:
        return max(wb.push(cfg, p) for p in rest)
    if cmd == "pull" and len(rest) == 2:
        return wb.pull(cfg, rest[0], rest[1])
    if cmd == "_watchdog":
        return wb.watchdog(cfg)
    print(__doc__)
    return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

The search covered RunPod's port exposure rules, but returned nothing on WebRTC, KasmVNC, Selkies, or RunPod desktop templates, so those parts of your query remain unanswered.

**What the results say about RunPod port exposure:**

- **UDP is not supported.** RunPod's overview says Pods only support TCP and HTTP connections. The docs advise that UDP-dependent apps be changed to use TCP instead (If your application relies on UDP, you'll need to modify your application to use TCP-based communication instead.). This matters for WebRTC, since its media transport normally relies on UDP.
- **HTTP proxy.** It is the default for web traffic. Click Edit Template and add a comma-separated list of ports to the Expose HTTP Ports (Max 10) field. Traffic is served at a URL built from the pod ID and port, and the proxy automatically provides HTTPS.
- **TCP exposure.** This gives a public IP with a mapped port. The docs say to use TCP port exposure with public IP addresses for services requiring direct TCP connections, lower latency, or protocols other than HTTP. For WebSockets, one doc notes that TCP exposure often works better for persistent connections that might exceed timeout limits.
- **Port mapping.** A port cannot be exposed as both HTTP and TCP at once (you cannot expose the same ports on both HTTP and TCP.). Public ports are assigned at runtime and are read from the Connect menu.

**Implications for a KasmVNC or Selkies desktop:** Both serve their browser clients over HTTP/WebSocket, so they should work through the HTTP proxy, though proxy timeouts on long-lived sockets are a possible issue; TCP exposure is the fallback. Selkies' WebRTC media path is the piece most likely to be affected by the no-UDP rule. I did not verify this, and the search found no RunPod-specific guidance on it. A further search on KasmVNC, Selkies, or WebRTC with RunPod, or on RunPod's own desktop templates, would be needed to confirm.

#!/bin/bash
# Prepare a fresh pod for rendering. Everything expensive is cached on the network
# volume, so this is slow once and fast forever after.
set -euo pipefail
VERSION="${1:?blender version, e.g. 4.5.14}"
SERIES="${VERSION%.*}"
VOL=/workspace
BLENDER_DIR="$VOL/blender/$VERSION"

mkdir -p "$VOL/bin" "$VOL/jobs" "$VOL/frames"

# Blender runs headless but still links the X and GL client libraries. ffmpeg comes
# from the same apt call: Ubuntu's mirrors are a CDN and finish in seconds, where
# fetching a static build from a single host was taking 70 seconds of every job.
if ! dpkg -s libxi6 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
  apt-get update -qq
  apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends \
    libx11-6 libxi6 libxxf86vm1 libxfixes3 libxrender1 libxkbcommon0 libsm6 libgl1 \
    xz-utils curl ffmpeg rsync >/dev/null
fi

if [ ! -x "$BLENDER_DIR/blender" ]; then
  # Several pods can now share the volume at once (parallel jobs), so unpack beside the
  # final folder and move it into place in one step: a half-unpacked Blender is never seen.
  echo "RD_SETUP downloading Blender $VERSION"
  URL="https://download.blender.org/release/Blender$SERIES/blender-$VERSION-linux-x64.tar.xz"
  TMP="$BLENDER_DIR.part.$$"; mkdir -p "$TMP" "$(dirname "$BLENDER_DIR")"
  curl -fsSL "$URL" -o "/tmp/blender.$$.tar.xz"
  tar -xJf "/tmp/blender.$$.tar.xz" -C "$TMP" --strip-components=1
  rm -f "/tmp/blender.$$.tar.xz"
  if [ ! -x "$BLENDER_DIR/blender" ]; then rm -rf "$BLENDER_DIR"; mv "$TMP" "$BLENDER_DIR"; else rm -rf "$TMP"; fi
fi

# Prefer whatever apt just installed. The static build stays as a fallback for an
# image where apt has no ffmpeg, and lives on the volume so it is fetched once.
if command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ln -sf "$(command -v ffmpeg)" "$VOL/bin/ffmpeg"
elif [ ! -x "$VOL/bin/ffmpeg" ]; then
  echo "RD_SETUP apt had no ffmpeg, downloading a static build"
  curl -fsSL https://johnvansickle.com/ffmpeg/releases/ffmpeg-release-amd64-static.tar.xz -o /tmp/ff.tar.xz
  mkdir -p /tmp/ff && tar -xJf /tmp/ff.tar.xz -C /tmp/ff --strip-components=1
  mv /tmp/ff/ffmpeg /tmp/ff/ffprobe "$VOL/bin/" && rm -rf /tmp/ff /tmp/ff.tar.xz
fi

"$BLENDER_DIR/blender" --version | head -1
# Free intelligence for later: if the Linux build can encode video itself, the
# external ffmpeg can be dropped entirely. The macOS builds cannot.
"$BLENDER_DIR/blender" -b --factory-startup -noaudio --python-expr "
import bpy
try:
    bpy.context.scene.render.image_settings.file_format = 'FFMPEG'
    print('RD_SETUP blender_can_encode: yes')
except TypeError:
    print('RD_SETUP blender_can_encode: no')
" 2>/dev/null | grep blender_can_encode || true
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total --format=csv,noheader
echo "RD_SETUP ready"

"""Run a command with a hard time limit: python3 limited.py <seconds> <cmd...>. Exit 124 when it had to be killed."""
import os, signal, subprocess, sys
p = subprocess.Popen(sys.argv[2:], start_new_session=True)
try:
    sys.exit(p.wait(timeout=float(sys.argv[1])))
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
    print("LIMIT hit after", sys.argv[1], "s", flush=True)

=== up() and run()
def up(cfg, log=print):
    pods = _Pods(cfg)
    st = _load(cfg)
    if st:
        try:
            pod = pods.client.get_pod(st["pod_id"])
            if pod.get("status") == "RUNNING":
                log(f"WB already up: pod {st['pod_id']} {st['gpu']} ${st['rate']:.2f}/hr, "
                    f"up {(time.time() - st['started']) / 3600:.1f} h")
                _touch(cfg)
                return 0
        except runpod_api.RunPodError:
            pass
        _close(cfg, st, "found dead", log)
    day, month = _caps_left(cfg)
    if day < 1 or month < 1:
        log(f"WB refused: spend cap reached (today ${day:.2f} left, this month ${month:.2f} left). Nick raises caps in render.env.")
        return 2
    if _wb_left(cfg) < 0.5:
        log(f"WB refused: today's workbench cap is used (${float(cfg.get('WORKBENCH_DAY_CAP_USD', 6)):.2f}). Nick raises WORKBENCH_DAY_CAP_USD in render.env.")
        return 2
    pod, _ = pods._create("workbench", log)
    started = time.time()
    rate = float(pod.get("cost") or 0)
    st = {"pod_id": pod["id"], "gpu": (pod.get("gpu") or {}).get("id", "?"), "rate": rate,
          "started": started, "last_used": started, "target": None,
          "blender": f"/workspace/blender/{cfg['BLENDER_VERSION']}/blender"}
    _save(cfg, st)
    _spawn_watchdog(cfg)                                     # from here on the pod can never outlive its limits
    try:
        pod, target = pods._wait_ready(pod["id"], log)
        st["target"] = list(target)
        st["rate"] = float(pod.get("cost") or rate)
        _save(cfg, st)
        if os.environ.get("WB_NO_BLENDER"):                  # browser-canvas films need no Blender (2026-10-13)
            boot = ("mkdir -p /workspace && (command -v rsync >/dev/null && command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null || "
                    "(apt-get update -qq && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq rsync ffmpeg >/dev/null))")
        else:
            pods._copy(target, SCRIPTS / "pod_bootstrap.sh", "/root/pod_bootstrap.sh")
            boot = f"mkdir -p /workspace && bash /root/pod_bootstrap.sh {shlex.quote(cfg['BLENDER_VERSION'])}"
        if _ssh(pods, st, boot) != 0:
            raise RuntimeError("bootstrap failed")
    except Exception as exc:
        log(f"WB setup failed: {exc}")
        _close(cfg, _load(cfg), "setup failed", log)
        return 1
    _touch(cfg)
    log(f"WB up: pod {st['pod_id']} {st['gpu']} ${st['rate']:.2f}/hr; idle stop {IDLE_MINUTES} min, hard stop {MAX_HOURS} h")
    return 0

    def request(self, method, path, body=None, timeout=60):
        url = f"{self.base}{path}"
        data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method)
        req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {self.api_key}")
        req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        req.add_header("User-Agent", USER_AGENT)
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
                raw = resp.read().decode()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            detail = exc.read().decode()[:1200]
            raise RunPodError(f"{method} {path} -> HTTP {exc.code}: {detail}") from None
        except urllib.error.URLError as exc:
            raise RunPodError(f"{method} {path} -> cannot reach RunPod: {exc.reason}") from None
        return json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {}

    # --- pods ----------------------------------------------------------------
    def create_pod(self, body):
        return self.request("POST", "/pods", body)

    def get_pod(self, pod_id):
        return self.request("GET", f"/pods/{pod_id}")

    def list_pods(self):
        out = self.request("GET", "/pods")
        return out if isinstance(out, list) else out.get("pods", out.get("data", []))

    def terminate_pod(self, pod_id):
        return self.request("DELETE", f"/pods/{pod_id}")

def push(cfg, local, log=print):
    st = _need(cfg, log)
    if not st:
        return 2
    local = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(local))     # not resolve(): /tmp must stay /tmp on the pod
    pods = _Pods(cfg)
    if Path(local).is_dir():
        _ssh(pods, st, f"mkdir -p {shlex.quote(local)}")
        rc = _rsync(pods, st, local + "/", local + "/", up=True, excludes=EXCLUDE)
    else:
        _ssh(pods, st, f"mkdir -p {shlex.quote(str(Path(local).parent))}")
        rc = _rsync(pods, st, local, local, up=True)
    _touch(cfg)
    return rc


def pull(cfg, remote, local, log=print):
    st = _need(cfg, log)
    if not st:
        return 2
    Path(local).expanduser().mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) if remote.endswith("/") else None
    rc = _rsync(_Pods(cfg), st, remote, str(Path(local).expanduser()) + ("/" if remote.endswith("/") else ""), up=False)
    _touch(cfg)
    return rc


---
def _ssh(pods, st, command, capture=False):
    target = tuple(st["target"])
    env = f"export BLENDER={shlex.quote(st['blender'])}; "
    if capture:
        return subprocess.run(pods._ssh_base(target) + [env + command], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return subprocess.run(pods._ssh_base(target) + [env + command]).returncode


def _rsync(pods, st, src, dst, up=True, excludes=()):
    host, port, user = st["target"]
    ssh = f"ssh -i {shlex.quote(str(pods.key))} -p {port} -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o LogLevel=ERROR"
    args = ["rsync", "-az", "-e", ssh] + [f"--exclude={e}" for e in excludes]
    pair = [src, f"{user}@{host}:{dst}"] if up else [f"{user}@{host}:{src}", dst]
    return subprocess.run(args + pair).returncode

**It is live now, until 09:50 your time.** Reload the page in your Chrome, open Navy shots, and press Generate scene on each shot: the right side is the real Blender, and it switches scene as you move between shots.

```bash
open -a "Google Chrome" http://localhost:8575/animate.html
```

**What I tested myself, through the page**
- **All four built scenes open** (dock, officer, cruiser, carrier), each looking through its own camera.
- **Saving works:** I moved something in the officer scene, a copy appeared within 30 seconds (`officer_v001.blend`), reached the box within a minute, and came back when I left the scene and returned. I deleted my test copies, so you start from the built scenes.
- **Loading steps:** opening a scene shows Blender's own steps with a moving bar, for example "Saving your work on the dock scene", "Loading the built officer scene", "Making your own working copy". The top line then shows "saved 08:40 · copy 1".
- **Cost:** about $0.13 so far at $0.89 an hour; the session ends by itself at 09:50, about $1.20 in total.

**Not done**
- The loading steps cover opening a scene only. The 5 minute machine start has no bars yet, because I still start the machine by hand.
- The 3D view is again drawn by the processor, not the graphics card.
- Nothing is committed.

**The live model and the chat**

Your reason changes my earlier advice: a chat that corrects the model while it builds belongs on this page. It is also the best training record you can get, because every correction is stored next to the exact change it caused.

```
animator types "the crane is too tall"
        -> model changes the crane in the live Blender
        -> you watch it change, and can say "stop"
        -> saved: the instruction + the before and after scene
```

- **What is missing today:** Generate opens a scene that was already finished yesterday. Nothing is built while you watch. For real time, the build has to run inside this live Blender in small visible steps.
- **The decision I need from you** is which model does that building. My pick is PlotPointe's own (GPT-6 Astra, the one the bot already runs on), since your second goal is to train PlotPointe to build these itself.
- **To verify before I promise it:** that the box's model can be pointed at the live Blender without disturbing the live bot. I have not checked that.

Based on: my own test in the page just now, the live Blender's status answers, and the files in `/Users/nick/plotpointe-live/saves` on the box.

# Imagine — Visual Creation Suite

## Modules
Call read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance:
- `diagram` — SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams
- `mockup` — UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards
- `interactive` — interactive explainers with controls
- `chart` — charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth)
- `art` — illustration and generative art
Pick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance.

**Complexity budget — hard limits:**
- Box subtitles: ≤5 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below — not the box.
- Colors: ≤2 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp.
- Horizontal tier: ≤4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes → shrink to ≤110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams.

If you catch yourself writing "click to learn more" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything.

**Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `<h2 class="sr-only">` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `<title>` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.)

You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat.

## Core Design System

These rules apply to ALL use cases.

### Philosophy
- **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins.
- **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces.
- **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text.
- **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it.

### Streaming
Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early.
- **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last.
- **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately.
- Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream.
- Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS.
- Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead.

### Rules
- No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming)
- No font-size below 11px
- No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths.
- No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects
- No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg)
- **Typography**: The default font is the person's Interface font, usually Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `fon ...[cut]

### CLAUDE 2026-11-13T07:25

**Reload the page (Cmd+R): the shot screen now starts empty, with the chat on the left and one button.** The two pictures I sent show it at the start and with Blender live.

**What changed**
- **Clear direction:** a shot opens with an empty Blender area and a single button, Generate scene. Press it and the real Blender takes that space.
- **Left is the chat,** empty until you write. All the old text is gone from there.
- **Three toggles, top right:** Chat (open), Shots and Details (both minimised). Flipping them does not reload Blender.
- **The shots strip** was there to jump between the storyboard's shots. It is now a thin line, "Shot 1 of 4" with two arrows; the pictures only show when you switch Shots on.
- **Details** holds everything that used to crowd the left: scene file, what is in the scene, build notes, checks.
- **Blender's window is cleaner:** the grey noVNC toolbar on its left edge is gone.

**The chat is real**
- Write in the page, for example "make the crane taller". It reaches this Claude, I build the change inside the live Blender, and the chat shows the step I am on with a moving bar and a Stop button.
- Stop works because I am refused my next step whenever you have written something I have not read.
- Every line is stored next to the saved copy number, so each instruction sits beside the scene before and after it.
- I act on chat lines only to change the open scene in the live Blender, nothing else.

**Tested by me:** a test line from the page reached me, my answer appeared in the page, a request pretending to come from another website was refused, and all four scenes still open. I then cleared my test lines. I have not yet made a real scene change from a chat line; your first message will be the first.

**Where things stand**
- Live until 10:08, $0.74 spent so far.
- Your two saved copies are kept (dock copy 1, officer copy 1); the dock opens from yours.
- Blender shows its welcome picture after each restart; one click on it closes it.
- All 55 page checks pass. Nothing is committed.

cat > \"$S/step_colour2.py\" <<'EOF'\nimport bpy\nimport numpy as np\ndone = []\n# Cloth: the builder's own tint is the colour the last Mix node adds (navy for jacket and trousers, white for the shirt).\nfor m in bpy.data.materials:\n    nodes = m.node_tree.nodes if m.node_tree else []\n    bsdf = next((n for n in nodes if n.type == \"BSDF_PRINCIPLED\"), None)\n    if not bsdf or not bsdf.inputs[\"Base Color\"].is_linked:\n        continue\n    src = bsdf.inputs[\"Base Color\"].links[0].from_node\n    if src.type == \"MIX\" and not src.inputs[\"B\"].is_linked and \"HG_Control\" in nodes:\n        col = None\n        for i in src.inputs:\n            if i.name == \"B\" and i.type == \"RGBA\":\n                col = i.default_value[:]\n        if col:\n            m.diffuse_color = col\n            done.append((m.name, [round(c, 3) for c in col[:3]]))\n# Skin: the average colour of the skin picture itself (dark empty parts of the picture left out).\nskin = bpy.data.materials.get(\".Human\")\nimg = bpy.data.images.get(\"Male 05.png\")\nif skin and img and img.size[0]:\n    px = np.empty(img.size[0] * img.size[1] * 4, dtype=np.float32)\n    img.pixels.foreach_get(px)\n    px = px.reshape(-1, 4)[::97, :3]\n    px = px[px.sum(axis=1) > 0.3]\n    col = [float(c) for c in px.mean(axis=0)] + [1.0]\n    skin.diffuse_color = col\n    done.append((skin.name, [round(c, 3) for c in col[:3]]))\nfor name, col in ((\".HG_Eyes_Inner\", (0.85, 0.85, 0.85, 1.0)), (\".HG_Teeth\", (0.8, 0.77, 0.7, 1.0))):\n    if bpy.data.materials.get(name):\n        bpy.data.materials[name].diffuse_color = col\n        done.append((name, col[:3]))\nfor a in bpy.context.window.screen.areas:\n    if a.type == \"VIEW_3D\":\n        a.spaces.active.shading.color_type = \"MATERIAL\"\nfor row in done:\n    print(row)\nEOF\npython3 tools/live/model.py step \"Colouring the jacket, shirt and skin\" \"$S/step_colour2.py\"; - tool `Write`: `{"file_path": "/Users/nick/Projects/plotpointe-animate/tools/live/view_colours.py", "content": "\"\"\"Runs inside the live Blender each time a shot is opened (pp_live.py), and can be sent as a build step.\n\nBlender's fast drawing mode paints every material in its \"viewport colour\". The built scenes leave that at plain grey,\nso the cast looks black and white. This gives each material the colour its own shader already has:\n\n  a plain shader colour            that colour\n  cloth from the character kit     the tint the builder mixed in last (navy jacket, white shirt)\n  skin                             the average colour of the skin picture\n  eyes and teeth                   white and ivory\n\nThe materials come from the shared library files, which a scene cannot write to, so this is done again on every open.\n\"\"\"\nimport bpy\nimport numpy as np\n\ncoloured = []\nfor m in bpy.data.materials:\n    nodes = m.node_tree.nodes if m.node_tree else []\n    bsdf = next((n for n in nodes if n.type == \"BSDF_PRINCIPLED\"), None)\n    if not bsdf:\n        continue\n    base = bsdf.inputs[\"Base Color\"]\n    colour = None\n    if not base.is_linked:\n        colour = base.default_value[:]\n    else:\n        last = base.links[0].from_node\n        tint = next((i for i in last.inputs if i.name == \"B\" and i.type == \"RGBA\"), None) if last.type == \"MIX\" else None\n        if tint and not tint.is_linked and \"HG_Control\" in nodes:\n            colour = tint.default_value[:]\n    skin = nodes.get(\"Color\") if m.name.startswith(\".Human\") else None\n    if skin and skin.type == \"TEX_IMAGE\" and skin.image and skin.image.size[0]:\n        px = np.empty(skin.image.size[0] * skin.image.size[1] * 4, dtype=np.float32)\n        skin.image.pixels.foreach_get(px)\n        px = px.reshape(-1, 4)[::97, :3]\n        px = px[px.sum(axis=1) > 0.3]                 # the empty, dark parts of the picture are left out\n        if len(px):\n            colour = [float(c) for c in px.mean(axis=0)] + [1.0]\n    if m.name.startswith(\".HG_Eyes_Inner\"):\n        colour = (0.85, 0.85, 0.85, 1.0)\n    if m.name.startswith(\".HG_Teeth\"):\n        colour = (0.8, 0.77, 0.7, 1.0)\n    if colour:\n        m.diffuse_color = colour\n        coloured.append(m.name)\nfor area in bpy.context.window.screen.areas:\n    if area.type == \"VIEW_3D\":\n        area.spaces.active.shading.color_type = \"MATERIAL\"\nprint(\"materials shown in their own colour:\", len(coloured))\n"}`

### CLAUDE 2026-11-13T07:47

**Both are in: reload the page once (Cmd+R) and try it.** Blender now draws on the graphics card, and my actions show on screen with a ring, the step's name, and a view that glides in and back. The two pictures I sent show it.

**Smoother**
- **Drawing:** 90 pictures a second in the officer scene, up from 26. Same test before and after (30 forced redraws). The cause was the processor drawing the view; one Blender setting moved it to the RTX 4090.
- **Shorter route:** the picture now goes straight from the machine to your Mac. It used to pass through the box, and that link dropped three times this morning.
- **What stays:** your internet's own delay to the machine, about a tenth of a second each way. I cannot remove that part.

**Showing what I do**
- When a step names the objects it touches, the view glides to them, a pulsing ring with the step's name marks them, the step runs, and the view glides back to the shot.
- Tested on the officer's cap badge: it zoomed in to the badge and returned to the full shot.

**Two fixes that came with it**
- The officer went grey again after a restart, because his materials live in the shared library file. Colours now apply by themselves every time a shot opens.
- The shot's camera frame now fills the view on every open.

**Things you should know**
- The app's safety check refused a download of an extra drawing tool to the rented machine. I did not work around it; Blender's own setting did the job with no download.
- For the direct line I added this Mac's public key to the rented machine. It disappears with the machine.
- My steps and tests pushed the officer to saved copy 9. Only copy 1 is yours.

### CLAUDE 2026-11-13T07:58

**The lag that is left comes from your internet connection, not from Blender.** Your Mac is on the Wi-Fi network called "iPhone", a phone hotspot, and I measured it.

| From your Mac to | Round trip |
|---|---|
| Your router (the phone) | 4.5 ms |
| A big public server nearby | 25 ms |
| The rented machine | 95 ms at best, 163 ms on average, 742 ms at worst |

- **What that feels like:** every mouse move takes a tenth to a fifth of a second to come back, with hiccups of up to three quarters of a second.
- **Blender itself is fast now:** 90 pictures a second on the graphics card, and the machine sat mostly idle while the timeline played.
- **The stream now delivers them:** my first reading was 15 pictures a second, and a few minutes later 28 a second, the full 24 a second of the playing timeline. I found two dead viewer connections left on the machine from when the line dropped at 09:47 and closed them; I cannot say for certain they caused the low first reading.
- **A machine somewhere else would not help:** from this connection every European region I tested answers in 80 to 115 ms.

**Correction:** I told you the delay was "a tenth of a second each way". It is about a tenth of a second for the whole round trip at best.

**What can still make it better**
- **Normal broadband or cable instead of the hotspot.** This is the big one and I cannot test it from here.
- **A lighter picture:** a smaller Blender window and lower picture quality, so more pictures get through a thin line. About one minute and one restart; it costs some sharpness.
- **A real video stream** made for this kind of use. It needs software downloaded onto the rented machine, which the app's safety check refused earlier, so it needs your say-so.

The timeline is stopped and back on frame 1, and Blender is yours again. My own extra viewer of the stream is closed; it was a second stream to your Mac while I was looking.

Live until 10:40, $1.23 spent so far. Nothing is committed.

### CLAUDE 2026-11-13T08:00

**Yes: stop sending pictures of Blender, and draw the scene inside the animator's own browser instead.** Then moving around costs no internet at all, and Blender only works in the background to build the scene and make the final clip.

**How it would work**
- Pressing Generate sends the browser a light copy of the scene, the same way a 3D model loads on a product website.
- The animator turns, zooms and moves things locally. It is instant, even on your hotspot.
- Only small changes travel, for example "officer moved 30 cm left" or "camera zoom ends at frame 200". Blender applies each one to the real scene and saves it.
- The graphics card is only rented for the final clip, not for the whole session.

**Why it also fits your other two goals**
- **Training PlotPointe:** every action arrives as a clean named change. That is a far better record than saved Blender files or a screen recording.
- **Slow laptops:** the light copy can be made as simple as the laptop needs.

**What it costs**
- We have to build each tool the animator uses ourselves. My guess at the order: look around, move and turn things, camera, timeline with play, and posing the character last, because that is the hard one.
- Anything outside those tools still needs the full Blender. I would keep today's streamed Blender behind an "Open full Blender" button for those cases.

You had a 3D viewer in the browser in the Blender Engine project in October. That folder is no longer on your Desktop and I have not looked for where it was archived, so I cannot say yet how much of it we can reuse.

🔴 **NEEDED:** what an animator actually does in one shot. My assumption is four things: pose the character, move things, set the camera, set the timing. If there is more, the list of tools grows.

The machine is still running until 10:40 at $0.89 an hour ($1.23 so far). Say "stop" if you are done with it for now.

### CLAUDE 2026-11-13T08:09

**Speed comes from not asking this Claude for everything, and quality comes from ready-made tools instead of fresh code each time.** The chart above shows the three lanes with the times I measured.

**Why it took so long**
- The chat's own clock: you wrote at 10:03:40, my first answer came at 10:04:38, and the face was done at 10:05:54. That is 2 minutes 14 seconds.
- This Claude is a general assistant that gets woken by your message, carries this whole long conversation, and was busy closing Blender's side panels when your line arrived.
- For each request I first inspect the scene, then write new Blender code, then check it. That is three round trips for something as simple as a zoom.

**How to get it fast**
1. **Buttons for the moves you make all the time,** with no AI in the way: zoom to the face, back to the camera, show or hide the bones, play. These are instant.
2. **A small Claude that does only this job.** It gets your line plus a short list of what is in the scene, and picks one ready-made tool. I tested it on this Mac with your own login: 4.3 to 5.1 seconds, and it picked the right objects for "zoom in on his face" all four times.
3. **This Claude only for big jobs** that no tool covers yet. It says so at once and shows its steps.

**Where the quality comes from**
- Each tool is written and tested once, like the face fix and the cap-badge zoom today. The small model only chooses a tool and its target; it never invents Blender code.
- When a request fits no tool, the big model solves it once and that solution becomes a new tool. This is also your second goal: PlotPointe learning to do it itself.

**Limits I can state now**
- About 5 seconds is the floor with the command-line route I tested. Going lower needs a model called directly with a paid key; I have not tested that.
- On your hotspot the picture itself still arrives with the delay we measured, whatever the model does.

Building this needs the machine for testing, roughly another hour, about $0.90. The current session ends at 10:40 and is at $1.35.

### CLAUDE 2026-11-13T08:40

**The quick lane is live: reload the page (Cmd+R) and try it.** The two pictures I sent show the buttons in use.

**What I measured, from your Mac over your hotspot**

| You do | Time |
|---|---|
| Press a button (Face, Full shot, Bones, Play, Undo) | 0.3 to 0.7 s |
| Type a plain command ("stop", "undo", "show the bones") | about 3 s |
| Type a normal line ("move him one metre to the left", "turn him around", "go to frame 100") | 9 to 12 s |
| Before today: any line, via the big assistant | 134 s |

**How it works**
- **Buttons** are ready-made tools inside Blender, with no AI in between. Move, turn, scale, frame, view mode and focus are built too, for the typed lines to use.
- **A small model** reads each typed line and picks a tool. It never writes Blender code, and every tool and number is checked before it runs.
- **The big assistant (me)** only gets lines nothing fits, such as colours, adding things or animating. The chat says so at once, and I pick it up.

### CLAUDE 2026-11-13T08:50

**Your line never reached Blender, and the page hid that. Reload the page (Cmd+R) and it can no longer hide it.**

**What happened**
- Blender's own chat log has no line from you after 10:35.
- At 10:44:41 the direct connection from your Mac to the machine dropped, which is likely your hotspot. Your message was lost in that gap.
- The page had already cleared your text and showed nothing, so it looked like it had vanished.

**What changed**
- **Your line shows the moment you send it,** marked "Sending…".
- **Once Blender has it,** the mark disappears and Blender's own copy of the line takes its place. After that the model's reply or its working bar follows.
- **If the connection is down,** the line stays in the chat as "Not sent. The line to Blender is down." with a "Try again" button, so you never retype it.
- **Nothing hangs any more:** every request to Blender gives up after 7 to 9 seconds, so a dead line shows within seconds.
- **Reconnecting is faster:** the tunnel from your Mac now notices a drop in about 12 seconds (it was 60) and reopens by itself.

**Tested live just now:** I typed "show the bones" in the page. It appeared at once as "Sending…", turned into Blender's copy, and "Bones shown." came back in about 3 seconds. I then hid the bones again. The two failure cases ("Not sent" and "Sending…") are covered by new checks; all 78 page checks pass.

**What I cannot fix:** if your hotspot drops, the connection still breaks. It will now say so within seconds and let you resend with one click, instead of staying silent.

const url = (location.protocol === "https:" ? "wss" : "ws") + "://" + location.host + "/websockify";
function connect() {
  const rfb = new RFB(document.getElementById("screen"), url);
  rfb.resizeSession = true;     // the machine's screen takes the size of this window, so Blender fills it at normal size
  rfb.scaleViewport = true;     // until the machine has resized, and if it cannot, the picture is scaled to fit
  rfb.addEventListener("disconnect", () => setTimeout(connect, 1500));
}

### CLAUDE 2026-11-13T08:56

**Yes: reload the page (Cmd+R) and Blender now fills its whole area at normal size.** The picture I sent shows it with Chat switched off.

**Why it looked small**
- The machine drew a fixed 1600×900 screen, and the page shrank it to fit your window. That left black bars and made every button and menu smaller than normal.

**What changed**
- **The machine's screen now takes the exact size of your page's Blender area.** Nothing is shrunk, so Blender looks the way it does on a normal laptop.
- **Blender is full screen inside that area:** no title bar and no black bars.
- **The page gives it more room:** less padding and no frame around it.
- **Chat off gives it the full width.** The screen resizes again by itself in about two seconds.
- **Lighter on your connection:** the picture is now exactly the size you see, instead of a large one shrunk down.

**Checked live:** I resized the area twice (Chat on, Chat off) and Blender re-laid itself out each time. All page checks pass.

**What to know**
- On a very wide window the machine sends a bigger picture, which costs more of your hotspot. If it feels slower, use a narrower window or keep Chat on.
- The setting applies from the next Blender restart by itself; today's session already has it.
- Blender's welcome picture still appears after a restart until one click.

Live until 11:28. $2.10 spent at 10:56; to the end it comes to about $2.50 today. Nothing is committed.

**Yes: one folder per script, named with its title, with numbered subfolders in pipeline order. The picture shows the layout next to what exists today.**

**What I read today**
- **Drive, "Art Of War Scripts":** about 30 script docs sitting flat in one folder, plus a "Published Scripts" folder. Storyboards, blends and clips are not there.
- **Drive root:** a separate "Blender Renders" folder that looked empty from here.
- **PlotPointe's data on the box:** every script is stored under its Google Doc id, for example the Bat Bombs storyboard under `1Zgi5YYJ…json`, not under its title.

**What I recommend**
- **A folder alone does not consolidate your operations.** You also want one record per script, "00 Record", that lists what exists: doc, storyboard, which blend copy is the latest, clip, sound, captions. The PlotPointe home page can then show every script with its pieces ticked off.
- **PlotPointe tracks each script by its Google Doc id** and keeps the folder next to it. The folder is named with the title for people, and a renamed title never breaks anything.
- **PlotPointe creates the folder by itself** when a script is approved, so nobody makes folders by hand.
- **The Animate page saves blend copies straight into "03 Blend".** Today they sit on the box and on this Mac.

**What I have not checked**
- Whether PlotPointe's bot has permission to create Drive folders. It reads docs today.
- Whether the animators' computers can sync a Drive folder with the large blend files; the officer file alone is about 227 MB.

**Your rule:** my standing rule lets me write to Drive only inside Nick-AE, and "Art Of War Scripts" is outside it. That is why I suggest a pilot with The Bat Bombs inside Nick-AE first. Moving a folder later in Drive is easy.

🔴 **NEEDED:** besides script, storyboard, blends, clips, sound and captions, what else does a script need? Your "etc." decides the subfolder list. Send your next question when ready.

"""PreToolUse gate: turns Nick's damage rules into checks (Boris: a mistake becomes a check, not a prompt).

**What I propose** (the sketch above)
- Replace the Google Doc on the desk with PlotPointe's own script box: you type in it directly, with **strikethrough, highlight and bold** buttons.

- Keep the chat, Undo and Approve as they are.
- On the new Scripts page, "Approve script" goes away; step 1 opens this desk instead. That stops the two pages repeating each other.

def _mark(tr):
    """Struck text as ~~cut~~, bold text as **the writer's own words**."""
    c, st = tr.get("content", ""), tr.get("textStyle", {})
    if not c.strip():
        return c
    if st.get("strikethrough"):
        return f"~~{c.strip()}~~ "
    if st.get("bold"):
        return f"**{c.strip()}** "
    return c


def _paras(body):
    out = []
    for el in body.get("content", []):
        p = el.get("paragraph")
        if p:
            t = "".join(_mark(r.get("textRun", {})) for r in p.get("elements", [])).strip()
            if t:
                out.append(t)
    return out


COLOURS = {"fluff": (1, .75, .4), "flow": (.62, .77, 1), "sense": (1, .6, .6), "keep": (.6, .9, .6), None: (1, .93, .62)}   # None is the agent's own yellow
VERSION_HEAD = re.compile(r"(?i)version\s*\d+(\W+final)?|final(\s+version)?")


def _colour(rgb):
    c = [rgb.get(k, 0) for k in ("red", "green", "blue")]
    return min(COLOURS, key=lambda k: sum((a - b) ** 2 for a, b in zip(c, COLOURS[k])))


def _colours(body):
    """What the writer coloured, each with the number of the version it sits in. Kept apart from the text, so finding and matching text never sees it."""
    out, version = [], 0
    for el in body.get("content", []):
        p = el.get("paragraph")
        if not p:
            continue
        if VERSION_HEAD.fullmatch("".join(r.get("textRun", {}).get("content", "") for r in p.get("elements", [])).strip()):
            version += 1
            continue
        last = None
        for r in p.get("elements", []):
            tr = r.get("textRun", {})
            rgb = tr.get("textStyle", {}).get("backgroundColor", {}).get("color", {}).get("rgbColor")
            label = _colour(rgb) if rgb and tr.get("content", "").strip() and not tr.get("textStyle", {}).get("strikethrough") else None
            if label and label == last:
                out[-1]["text"] += tr["content"]
            elif label:
                out.append({"label": label, "text": tr["content"], "version": version})
            last = label
    for c in out:
        c["text"] = c["text"].strip()
    return out

**The plan is drawn above. One thing I found changes it: PlotPointe already reads your writers' formatting as feedback.** This is in the live code as of today; the page is unchanged since 11 Nov.

| In the doc | PlotPointe reads it as |
|---|---|
| Strikethrough | cut this |
| Bold | the writer's own words |
| Orange highlight | fluff |
| Blue highlight | flow |
| Red highlight | doesn't make sense |
| Green highlight | keep |
| Yellow | PlotPointe's own suggestion |

So the new script box keeps exactly these meanings. Its buttons are named by meaning (Cut, My words, Fluff, Flow, Sense, Keep), not by colour, and nothing the writers already do is lost.

**Decision 1 of 3: where the script lives**
- **A. The doc stays underneath, out of sight** (my pick). Writers only ever see the box in PlotPointe. Each change is saved to the doc behind the scenes, so the chat's edits, Undo, Compare drafts and "Saving what we learned" all keep working from day one. Example: you strike "so the pilot could see again" in the box. PlotPointe records it, and the doc underneath gets the same strikethrough.
- **B. No doc at all.** PlotPointe holds the text alone. Cleaner later, but the chat's editing, Undo and Compare drafts are all built on the doc today, so they would have to be rebuilt before writers could use it.

**Coming next, one at a time:**
2. What counts as one recorded change. My pick: every pause in typing, plus every chat change and every Undo.
3. How we try it safely. My pick: a test copy of PlotPointe on its own address, tried on one script, then switched live only on your "ship".

### CLAUDE 2026-11-13T10:14

**Decision 1 is set: PlotPointe holds the script itself, with no Google Doc behind it, and each script's Drive folder gets an updated copy.**

**What that means**
- **The Drive copy:** "01 Script" in each script's folder gets a readable copy, rewritten every time a change is recorded, so Drive is never behind.
- **The cost:** the chat's editing, Undo, Compare drafts and the "Saving what we learned" step all work on the Google Doc today. They have to be rebuilt to work on PlotPointe's own text. That is the biggest part of this job.
- **Starting text:** each of the 26 scripts starts from the latest version in its doc today, read once. Example: "He Told His Own Guns to Fire on Him" starts from its "Version 1" tab. Its "Fun Facts", "Feedback & Lessons" and "Changes Comparison" tabs are not part of the script.

**Decision 2 of 3: what counts as one recorded change**
- **Every pause in typing (my pick):** about two seconds without a keystroke closes one change. Example: you strike six words and stop, and the record gets "11:42, Nick, cut 'so the pilot could see again'". Every chat change and every Undo is recorded the same way. This gives the platform the most to learn from.
- **Only on save:** one change each time someone presses Save. Fewer, bigger entries, but you lose the order in which things were changed.

### CLAUDE 2026-11-13T10:21

**Got it: logging runs in work sessions.** A session starts at the first activity on a script, stops after 5 minutes with no activity, and the next activity starts a new one.

**Example:** you open "He Carried the Burning Bomb" at 11:40 and edit until 11:52. At 11:57, with nothing for 5 minutes, the record closes **"Session 1: 11:40 to 11:52, Nick, 14 changes"**. You come back at 14:05 and type, and Session 2 starts.

Inside a session, every change is still logged: each pause in typing, each chat change, each Undo. That way the platform sees both how long people work and what they change. Say so if you meant only the session itself, without the individual changes.

**Decision 3 of 3: trying it safely**
- **Test copy first (my pick):** a second copy of PlotPointe on its own address on the same box. Writers keep using today's version untouched. You and I try the new script desk on one script, for example "He Carried the Burning Bomb". Only after your "ship" does the live PlotPointe switch.
- **Straight to live:** faster, but writers would see half-finished work, and a mistake could interrupt them mid-script.

- **Every finished step has a "Reopen" button** (the script's says "Reopen to edit"). The script goes back to editing; a reopened storyboard goes back to waiting for approval.

- **Approval never locks** is now a rule for the real build too. In the new desk, reopening is recorded in the log like any other change.
