**The chat is on every script's page: reload (Cmd+R) and open a script.** The picture I sent shows it after a real request.

**How it works**
- Under the script box there is a line: "Tell PlotPointe what to change".
- The model edits the script **in the box itself**, then says in a sentence or two what it changed and why.
- The reply shows the old line struck through next to the new one, with an **Undo** button.
- A question gets an answer and leaves the script alone.
- Every chat edit and every Undo goes into the change list, and the whole chat is saved in the script's Drive folder under "00 Record".

**What I tested, with the real model**

| I typed | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| "the last line is too long, cut it down to the explosion and what it destroyed" | Last line became "until the explosives finally went off, destroying the gates." The other six lines stayed word for word. | 10 s |
| "why did you remove the part about the rest of the war?" | It explained, and did not touch the script. | 7 s |
| Undo | The original last line came back, and the log shows the Undo. | instant |

I removed my test chat and edits afterwards. All 143 checks pass.

**What the model follows**
- Your own house rules from PlotPointe: I copied the 15 craft rules, the banned hedges and "no years" read-only from the live system.
- Your marks: it knows what Cut, My words, Fluff, Flow, Sense and Keep mean, so "apply my marks" should work. I have not tested that request yet.
- It changes only what you ask for, and has no tools; it can only answer.

**What to know**
- **Which model:** a Claude (Sonnet) on your own login, run by the page's server on this Mac. It is not PlotPointe's own model, so its writing may differ from what the live bot produces.
- **While it works, the box is locked,** so your typing cannot be overwritten.
- **On an approved script the chat is off** until you press "Reopen to edit".
- The live PlotPointe is untouched, and nothing is committed.

def all_states(work=WORK, scripts=None):
    scripts = scripts if scripts is not None else registry()
    out = {}
    for folder in scripts:
        f = work / f"{folder}.json"
        if f.is_file():
            out[folder] = json.loads(f.read_text())
    return out


class Page(SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kw):
        super().__init__(*args, directory=str(ROOT), **kw)

    def end_headers(self):
        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
        super().end_headers()

    def answer(self, code, data):
        body = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        self.send_response(code)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_GET(self):
        if urlparse(self.path).path == "/api/state":
            return self.answer(200, {"scripts": all_states()})
        return super().do_GET()

    def do_POST(self):
        url = urlparse(self.path)
        origin = self.headers.get("Origin")
        if url.path not in ("/api/save", "/api/chat", "/api/new") or (origin and origin not in PAGES):
            return self.answer(403, {"error": "not allowed"})
        size = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        if size > 2_000_000:
            return self.answer(413, {"error": "too large"})
        folder = parse_qs(url.query).get("folder", [""])[0]
        try:
            body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(size))
            if url.path == "/api/chat":
                return self.answer(200, chat(folder, body))
            if url.path == "/api/new":
                return self.answer(200, new_script(body))
            written = save(folder, body)
        except (ValueError, OSError) as exc:
            return self.answer(400, {"error": str(exc)})
        return self.answer(200, {"ok": True, "written": written})

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"PlotPointe preview on http://localhost:{PORT}/animate.html", flush=True)
    ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), Page).serve_forever()

### CLAUDE 2026-11-13T17:45

I built James's demo: a cover page plus one page for each of the 7 checkpoints. The platform now tracks all 7 steps too: idea, script, storyboard, preview, SFX, captions and publish. All 193 checks pass, I checked it in the browser at 20:00 on 13 Nov, and nothing is shipped or committed.

- **Your part:** in Ideas, click **New idea** and write the title and idea. Approve it, then write the script in the box. For the storyboard, put the pictures in the script's **02 Storyboard** folder in Drive, named in shot order. They then show on the script page and in the demo.
- **My part:** the preview goes in **04 Clips**, the sound in **05 Sound**, the captions file in **06 Captions** and the final video in **07 Publish**. The demo plays each one from its folder. I tested this with throwaway test files and real Drive was not touched.
- **Until your script exists**, the demo shows The Captain Who Sank His Own Ship. Pages it has nothing for yet say so plainly, for example "No sound yet."
- **Work already saved is kept:** He Carried the Burning Bomb still has its script reopened and its storyboard approved.

🔴 **FLAG:** the demo links into the platform, so it only works on this Mac while the preview server runs. To show it to James anywhere else it has to be deployed, and that only happens on your "ship".

Open it at http://localhost:8575/demo.html.

### CLAUDE 2026-11-14T07:28

The demo is now an onboarding flow. **Page 1 introduces PlotPointe, then each page is one step, with a progress bar on top.** All 194 checks pass, and I checked it on desktop and on a phone, where nothing scrolls sideways.

- **Page 1, Welcome:** one line on what PlotPointe does, then the 7 steps as a numbered path with one line each. Below that are 3 facts (7 steps, every edit recorded, 1 Drive folder per story) and a **Get started** button.
- **Top bar:** "Step 3 of 7" plus a 7-part progress bar. Finished steps are dimmer, the current step is bright, and you can click any part to jump to that step.
- **Each step page:** a number badge and a short action title like "Draw the storyboard". It also shows where that step stands in PlotPointe right now, one main picture, a few small "how it works" cards, and **Continue**.
- **Until your script exists**, the demo still shows the Captain. Steps with nothing made yet say so plainly.

Open it at http://localhost:8575/demo.html. It only runs on this Mac until you say "ship".

### CLAUDE 2026-11-14T09:31

**The demo now starts fresh:** it shows no other story and every step says "Not started", so it's ready for his story. All checks pass, and I clicked through it in the browser.

- **To start his story:** on any step, click **"Start the story in PlotPointe →"**. It opens the New idea form, where you add the title, the idea and the script.
- **It fills in by itself:** the newest story you write in PlotPointe becomes the demo's story, with its idea, script and edits. Your storyboard pictures in Drive show up on their pages too.
- **Showing an older story** is still possible with `?script=<folder>`, and `?fresh` always gives the empty version.
- **Try to make only one story in PlotPointe before the demo.** A test story made after his would take over the demo.

Open it at http://localhost:8575/demo.html.
